clue.text: Top team at a disadvantage, in total confusion

parts.note: up means at the top, as in 'up' on the hill
a side is a sports team
to be down is to be behind or losing, as in two goals down

explanation.surface: A leading sports team finds itself trailing and in complete disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned topsy-turvy is in utter disorder, so the phrase is an idiom for chaos.

clue.text: Raised money used at first for single item

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of used
raised in a down clue means written upwards, so the money word reads backwards

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash collected was spent first on one article.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is one individual thing counted on its own.

clue.text: Curiously notices division

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone oddly spots a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a part or segment into which something is divided.

clue.text: Gave proof of evil spirits, taunted principally and scolded

parts.note: demons are evil spirits

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of taunted

parts.note: to rate is an old word meaning to berate or scold

explanation.surface: Showed that devils exist, having mocked them and told them off.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold is an old-fashioned sense, unrelated to judging value.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to prove something by evidence or argument.

clue.text: In a high degree supporting quality food shop distribution

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so this word comes after the shop

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, sells fine foods
very means to a high degree

explanation.surface: A smart grocery's hand-out is highly backed.
explanation.definitionFit: Distribution, the handing out of goods, is the process of bringing them round.

clue.text: Cautious about tea mostly over-diluted

indicators.note: about means placed round, so the cautious word surrounds the shortened tea

parts.note: wary means cautious

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of tea that is too weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cautious' looks like part of the tea-drinking picture, but it supplies the outer word; 'mostly' and 'about' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinned with too much liquid, a weak drink is described as wishy-washy.

clue.text: Questions idiot about king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the idiot word wraps round the king letter

parts.note: an ass is a fool
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone interrogates a fool regarding the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone is to put queries to them, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Accounts of southern right-wingers

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: Reports of Conservatives from the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are narratives or tales of events.

clue.text: Incorporating art, working sappers produce replacement components

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so art goes inside the reworked letters
working means in operation, suggesting the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Military engineers, taking in some art, manufacture spare bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns SAPPERS into SPAREPS, which 'Incorporating' opens to take ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Spares are duplicate pieces kept to swap in when originals fail.

clue.text: Unfinished in short competition, allowed time finally

parts.note: comp is a common shortening of competition
let means permitted

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word time

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a brief contest was left incomplete, though time was eventually permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unfinished is lacking its completion, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Couch found in contents of attic

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An old couch discovered among the things stored in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading takes 'contents of attic' as an inside-letters signal, but the answer straddles the words: the S ending 'contents', then 'of' and the A of 'attic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is an upholstered seat for several people, the same piece of furniture.

clue.text: Makes sense of surprising realisations

indicators.note: surprising describes the realisations as unexpected, signalling their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone comes to terms with startling discoveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To rationalise is to explain logically, making something intelligible.

clue.text: Manner of one in workforce

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one within the word for workforce

parts.note: the men are the workers of a firm
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asks about the attitude of a single employee among the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing or demeanour, the way someone looks and carries themselves, is their manner.

clue.text: Awkward relatives might be able to adapt

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsily arranged, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Difficult family members might be capable of adjusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile turns easily to different tasks, which is being adaptable.

clue.text: Vehicles to drive with patience, it's said

definitions.text: Vehicles to drive with patience, it's said

parts.words: Vehicles to drive with patience, it's said
parts.note: said aloud, patience is the same as patients, the people these hospital vans carry

explanation.walkthrough: The surface urges calm driving; the pun is that 'patience' sounds like 'patients', so these are vehicles carrying the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency vans that take sick or injured people to hospital.

clue.text: Commons' terseness conceals fiendish things

indicators.note: conceals says the letters are held within the words before it

explanation.surface: Brevity in the House of Commons hides something wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsters are frightful, devilish creatures, so they fit fiendish things.

clue.text: Brief rest in rocky site in outskirts of sierra

indicators.note: the second in puts the shuffled site letters inside the edges of the next word
outskirts are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters of sierra
rocky means unsteady, telling us to rearrange the letters of site

explanation.surface: A short break on a stony patch at the edge of a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' reads as describing the site, but it is the anagram signal; 'outskirts of' keeps only the two ends of 'sierra'.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a short period of repose.

clue.text: Client of copper oddly swears about cat

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the odd letters wrap round the cat
oddly takes the letters in odd positions of swears

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A shopper made of copper curses at a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the chemical element; 'oddly' and 'about' work on 'swears' and 'cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a buyer or patron of a business.

clue.text: After uni cut short, boy goes round old dump

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter
goes round means the boy word surrounds the letter for old

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A student drops out early, and a young man ends up dumping things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' simply sets the shortened 'uni' first; 'dump' is a verb here, meaning to empty out a load.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump a cargo is to discharge it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Crime racket now and then between two US cities

indicators.note: between puts the picked letters in the gap separating the two cities

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles and NY is New York

indicators.note: now and then means every other letter of racket

explanation.surface: A criminal racket operating intermittently between two American cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests organised crime, which feeds the definition, but it is only the source of alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is a criminal offence, the legal name for stealing.

clue.text: Muslim with Parisian is most genial

parts.note: a Sunni is a member of the larger branch of Islam
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A Muslim in the company of a Frenchman proves the friendliest.
explanation.walkthrough: EST is French for 'is', so 'Parisian is' gives it; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheeriest, warmest disposition is the superlative of a bright, friendly temperament.

clue.text: Endless memos stir dons' agitation of mind

indicators.note: endless means losing both ends, applied to each of the three words in turn

explanation.surface: Constant memos rile the university dons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips each word to EMO, TI and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling stirs the mind, so an agitated state is a feeling.

clue.text: Lop off eel's head? That's harsh!

parts.note: to sever is to cut off

indicators.note: head is the first letter of eel

explanation.surface: Chopping off an eel's head seems cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe treatment is stern or harsh, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Male opponents involved in a welcome contract

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within the next word

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
E and N, East and North, are opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Men on opposing sides sign up to a friendly deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play East-West, so any east and north pair are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding arrangement between parties, a synonym.

clue.text: Curving branch of circling body of water

indicators.note: circling suggests turning round, so the water word is read backwards

parts.note: a pool is a small body of water

explanation.surface: A winding offshoot of a stream that bends round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A curving branch such as a railway or road offshoot rejoining the main line is a loop line.

clue.text: Favourites slowly walk up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means written upwards, so the walk word is reversed

parts.note: to step is to walk with paces

explanation.surface: Preferred ones amble upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Teacher's darlings are the favoured, preferred ones.

clue.text: Ship's propeller failing to start for those manning craft

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a screw is a ship's propeller

explanation.surface: A vessel's propeller breaks down, bad news for the sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailors who staff a boat are its company of hands.

clue.text: Unusually impressive, allowing freedom of behaviour

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters of the next word are reordered

explanation.surface: Something remarkably striking, yet lax in its rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient, tolerant attitude lets people do as they please.

clue.text: Very good ultimately dry area's leguminous plant

parts.note: so-so is middling, so plain so is used for very good in crosswords

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of dry

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A legume that ends up very good in a dry region.
explanation.definitionFit: The soybean is a bean-family crop, so it belongs among the legumes.

clue.text: Shows concerning gifts

parts.note: re means about or concerning
presents are gifts

explanation.surface: Displays relating to presents.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or portray something is to show it.
